## Why this paper exists

An AI student who wants a new research idea has to read a huge pile of papers, work out how a field developed, learn the background concepts those papers assume, and only then propose something feasible. The authors call this the **"information-to-innovation" gap**.

*GoAI* (Graph of AI Ideas) is their proposed tool. It builds a **knowledge graph** of papers and uses an LLM to search that graph. The output is a set of research trends, a learning path ordered by prerequisite, and "Hint Ideas" to spark the student's own thinking. A fine-tuned reviewer model then gives feedback on the student's ideas.

The paper is worth understanding for two reasons. Its central design argument is that research is a graph, not a list. And its evidence comes from a very small study, so you will need to judge how far that evidence goes.
